subject.title: [Security] Open redirect vulnerability in OAuth authorization callback handler

question: Does OpenClaw currently expose an OAuth authorization callback that redirects using caller-controlled destination input, and if so which component owns its redirect-origin policy?
rationale: The report names uncorroborated paths, while an actual OAuth redirect flaw would require security-sensitive ownership and threat-model judgment before a repair can be scoped safely.

options.title: Verify the callback boundary
options.body: Trace the active OAuth callback implementation and add a narrowly scoped allowlist or registered-redirect check only if user-controlled destination input reaches it.

options.title: Close as invalid after verification
options.body: Close only after source inspection confirms that no OpenClaw OAuth callback accepts or redirects to the alleged query parameter.

recommendation.title: Verify the callback boundary
recommendation.body: Trace the active OAuth callback implementation and add a narrowly scoped allowlist or registered-redirect check only if user-controlled destination input reaches it.

likelyOwner.reason: The reporter is the only identified person connected to the alleged surface; source-history ownership remains unestablished.
